title: Coral Reefs: The Underwater Cities That Feed, Protect, and Cure Us
title_zh: 珊瑚礁：养育、守护、治愈我们的海底城市
intro_zh: 本文约900词，介绍珊瑚礁为何重要，涵盖其生物多样性、渔业、海岸保护、经济与药物价值，以及面临的威胁和保护措施。

paragraphs.en: Beneath the blue waves, coral reefs often look like colorful gardens filled with fish. But they are much more than pretty scenes. Scientists call them the rainforests of the sea because they support an amazing diversity of life. For centuries, people have been drawn to their beauty, yet few realize how deeply our own lives depend on these underwater structures. In fact, coral reefs are essential to the health of the ocean and to human society in ways that are still being discovered.
paragraphs.zh: 在蔚蓝的波浪之下，珊瑚礁经常看起来像是充满鱼类的彩色花园。但它们远不止是美丽的景观。科学家称它们为海洋热带雨林，因为它们孕育着惊人的生命多样性。几个世纪以来，人们被它们的美吸引，却很少有人意识到我们自身的生活在多大程度上依赖这些水下结构。事实上，珊瑚礁对海洋健康以及人类社会至关重要，其重要性仍在不断被发现。

paragraphs.en: One of the most striking facts about coral reefs is their incredible biodiversity. Although reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, they are home to about twenty-five percent of all marine species. Thousands of types of fish, mollusks, crustaceans, and plants find food and shelter within these structures. A single reef can host more kinds of creatures than a whole tropical forest. This rich variety not only fascinates scientists but also keeps the ocean's food web balanced. When one species disappears, the whole system can suffer.
paragraphs.zh: 关于珊瑚礁，最令人惊叹的事实之一是其不可思议的生物多样性。尽管珊瑚礁只覆盖不到百分之一的海洋底部，却养育了大约百分之二十五的海洋物种。成千上万种鱼类、软体动物、甲壳类动物和植物在这些结构中寻找食物和庇护所。一个珊瑚礁可以容纳的生物种类比整片热带森林还要多。这种丰富的多样性不仅让科学家着迷，也维持着海洋食物网的平衡。当一个物种消失时，整个系统都会受损。

paragraphs.en: Coral reefs are also a vital source of food for millions of people. In many developing countries, coastal communities rely on reef fish as their main source of protein. According to the United Nations, about 500 million people live within 100 kilometers of a coral reef, and many depend on it for their livelihoods. Small-scale fishermen catch fish, crabs, and other seafood that feed families and support local markets. If reefs continue to decline, these communities would lose not only their income but also their daily meals. This is why protecting reefs is directly related to fighting hunger and poverty.
paragraphs.zh: 珊瑚礁也是数百万人重要的食物来源。在许多发展中国家，沿海社区依赖珊瑚礁鱼类作为主要蛋白质来源。据联合国统计，约五亿人生活在距离珊瑚礁一百公里以内的地区，其中许多人靠珊瑚礁维持生计。小规模渔民捕捞鱼类、螃蟹和其他海产品，养家糊口并支撑当地市场。如果珊瑚礁持续退化，这些社区不仅会失去收入，还会失去日常餐食。这就是为什么保护珊瑚礁直接关系到对抗饥饿和贫困。

paragraphs.en: In addition to providing food, coral reefs act as natural barriers that protect coastal areas from waves and storms. The rough structure of a reef breaks the energy of incoming waves, reducing their strength before they reach the shore. This protection helps prevent coastal erosion and reduces the damage caused by typhoons and hurricanes. For example, a healthy reef can lower the height of a storm wave by up to 70 percent. In this way, coral reefs save billions of dollars in flood damages every year. They are a cheaper and more effective solution than building concrete sea walls.
paragraphs.zh: 除了提供食物，珊瑚礁还充当天然屏障，保护沿海地区免受海浪和风暴的侵袭。珊瑚礁粗糙的结构能分解来袭海浪的能量，削弱其到达海岸前的强度。这种保护有助于防止海岸侵蚀，并减少台风和飓风造成的破坏。例如，健康的珊瑚礁可以将风暴浪高降低多达百分之七十。通过这种方式，珊瑚礁每年节省数十亿美元的洪水损失。它们比建造混凝土海堤更便宜、更有效。

paragraphs.en: Coral reefs bring enormous economic benefits through tourism and recreation. Diving, snorkeling, and underwater photography attract millions of travelers every year. The Great Barrier Reef in Australia, for instance, contributes more than 3 billion dollars annually to the country's economy. In many island nations, tourism is a leading industry, and the beauty of coral reefs is the main reason why visitors come. Local hotels, restaurants, boat operators, and guides all depend on healthy reefs. This means that protecting coral reefs is not only an environmental issue but also a smart economic investment.
paragraphs.zh: 珊瑚礁通过旅游业和休闲活动带来巨大的经济效益。潜水、浮潜和水下摄影每年吸引数百万游客。例如，澳大利亚的大堡礁每年为该国的经济贡献超过三十亿美元。在许多岛国，旅游业是支柱产业，而珊瑚礁的美景正是游客前来的主要原因。当地的酒店、餐厅、船只运营商和导游都依赖健康的珊瑚礁。这意味着保护珊瑚礁不仅是环境问题，也是一项明智的经济投资。

paragraphs.en: Perhaps the most surprising treasure of coral reefs is their medicinal potential. Many plants and animals that live on reefs produce chemical compounds that can be used to treat human diseases. For instance, some coral species have been used to create drugs for certain types of cancer, while others show promise in fighting infections and heart problems. Sponges and sea squirts found on reefs have also provided substances for new antibiotics. Scientists believe that many more life-saving medicines are waiting to be discovered in these underwater communities. If we destroy these reefs, we may lose cures for diseases that have not yet been solved.
paragraphs.zh: 也许珊瑚礁最令人惊喜的宝藏是它们的药用潜力。生活在珊瑚礁上的许多动植物会产生可用于治疗人类疾病的化学化合物。例如，一些珊瑚种类已被用于制造治疗某些癌症的药物，而其他珊瑚则显示出对抗感染和心脏问题的前景。在珊瑚礁上发现的海绵和海鞘也为新型抗生素提供了物质。科学家相信，还有更多救命的药物正等待在这些水下群落中被发现。如果我们毁掉这些珊瑚礁，就可能失去尚未被攻克的疾病的治疗方法。

paragraphs.en: Despite their importance, coral reefs are in serious danger. The biggest threat is climate change. When water temperatures rise, corals become stressed and expel the tiny algae that give them their color and energy. This process, known as coral bleaching, can kill entire reef systems. Pollution, overfishing, and destructive fishing practices also damage reefs rapidly. Studies show that nearly half of the world's coral reefs have already been lost or severely damaged. If current trends continue, up to 90 percent of reefs could die within the next few decades. This would cause a catastrophic loss of biodiversity, food supply, and coastal protection.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管珊瑚礁很重要，但它们正面临严重危险。最大的威胁是气候变化。当水温升高时，珊瑚会感到压力，并排出赋予它们颜色和能量的微小藻类。这个过程被称为珊瑚白化，可以杀死整个珊瑚礁系统。污染、过度捕捞和破坏性捕捞方式也迅速损害珊瑚礁。研究表明，世界上近一半的珊瑚礁已经消失或严重受损。如果当前趋势继续下去，在未来几十年内，高达百分之九十的珊瑚礁可能会死亡。这将导致生物多样性、食物供应和海岸保护的灾难性损失。

paragraphs.en: Fortunately, there is hope. Conservation efforts around the world are helping to restore damaged reefs. Marine protected areas, in which fishing and pollution are controlled, have shown positive results. Scientists are also experimenting with coral farming, planting new corals to replace dead ones. On an individual level, people can help by reducing carbon emissions, using sunscreens that are safe for marine life, and choosing sustainable seafood. Every small action can make a big difference. For example, choosing to walk or bike instead of driving reduces the carbon footprint that warms the ocean.
paragraphs.zh: 幸运的是，仍有希望。世界各地的保护工作正在帮助恢复受损的珊瑚礁。在禁止捕捞和控制污染的海洋保护区内，已经出现了积极的效果。科学家们还在尝试珊瑚养殖，种植新的珊瑚来替代死去的珊瑚。在个人层面，人们可以通过减少碳排放、使用对海洋生物安全的防晒霜以及选择可持续的海产品来提供帮助。每一个小行动都能带来大改变。例如，选择步行或骑自行车而不是开车，可以减少使海洋变暖的碳足迹。

paragraphs.en: In summary, coral reefs are not just beautiful places to visit; they are essential to the survival of both marine life and humans. They feed us, protect our shores, support economies, and may even hold the keys to future medicine. The ecosystem services they provide are irreplaceable and often unappreciated. As we face the challenges of climate change, safeguarding coral reefs should be a global priority. Every effort we make today will determine whether these underwater cities continue to thrive for future generations.
paragraphs.zh: 总之，珊瑚礁不仅是美丽的旅游胜地，更是海洋生物和人类生存的关键。它们为我们提供食物、守护海岸、支撑经济，甚至可能掌握着未来医学的钥匙。它们提供的生态系统服务是不可替代的，而且常常被忽视。当我们面临气候变化的挑战时，保护珊瑚礁应成为全球优先事项。我们今天所做的每一分努力，都将决定这些水下城市能否继续为子孙后代繁荣存在。

questions.q: What is the main purpose of this article?
options: To describe the beauty of coral reefs
To explain why coral reefs are important and deserve protection
To list the economic benefits of tourism
To discuss techniques of coral farming
questions.explain: 主旨题。文章从生物多样性、渔业、海岸保护、经济和医药价值等方面说明珊瑚礁的重要性，并呼吁保护，因此答案为B。

questions.q: According to the passage, coral reefs cover less than 1% of the ocean floor but support about ______ of all marine species.
questions.explain: 细节题。第二段明确提到“about twenty-five percent”，即25%，对应C选项。

questions.q: What can be inferred from the passage about losing coral reefs?
options: People may have less protein-rich food.
Coastal erosion may become more serious.
Some future medicines may be lost forever.
questions.explain: 推断题。文章指出珊瑚礁提供食物、海岸保护及药物资源，失去它们会导致这些方面受损，因此A、B、C都正确，选D。

questions.q: The word 'expel' in Paragraph 7 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 词义题。根据语境，珊瑚在压力下排出藻类，“expel”意为“排出、逐出”，与push out同义，故选A。
